# How do these specialised animal tissues connect across movable skeletal boundaries to produce coordinated movement?

Follow one signal from a neuron into a skeletal muscle cell. The muscle shortens exactly as expected.

Yet shortening alone cannot move a limb unless the pull is transmitted across a movable connection between bones.

The organism now possesses protective, supportive, contractile and signalling tissues, but it still lacks the mechanical arrangement that converts shortening into coordinated movement.
